nodes.label: Frontend stack plan
nodes.source_location: Frontend stack plan (mascot, micro-animations, UI motion)
nodes.rationale: Draft for review. Baseline is Expo SDK 57, React Native 0.86.3, React 19.2 with the React Compiler on, New Architecture only, Hermes V1, @react-navigation/native-stack 7, expo-image, react-native-svg, and react-native-worklets 0.10.1 already installed but unused. Scope is the full frontend stack. Dark mode is out of scope. iOS and Android are one Expo codebase, with the 2 GB Android phone as the performance gate.

nodes.label: Lottie-first mascot runtime
nodes.source_location: 1.1 Mascot + micro-animations: Lottie first (works in Expo Go), Rive deferred
nodes.rationale: Decision on 2026-10-23, superseding an earlier Rive-first recommendation. The owner chose Lottie because it runs in Expo Go without a dev build and the designer works only in Figma. lottie-react-native, Expo-bundled at about 7.3.8, is the primary runtime. Do not ship Lottie and Rive together by default, because two native runtimes add APK size and memory. Figma Motion exports keyframes and MP4, not Lottie JSON, so simple fades, slides, and presses are rebuilt in Reanimated, and mascot clips need LottieFiles or an After Effects pass. A cheaper idle float can be layered static art plus Reanimated, with Lottie only for richer clips such as success, loader, and confetti. Revisit Rive only if mood transitions are too awkward as hard-cut clips.

nodes.label: Rive
nodes.source_location: 1.1 Mascot + micro-animations: Lottie first (works in Expo Go), Rive deferred
nodes.rationale: Original recommendation for the state-driven mascot, because state machines and small .riv files suit 2 GB devices. Deferred. @rive-app/react-native uses the Nitro runtime, needs a dev build, and is not in Expo Go. It wants New Architecture and React Native >= 0.78. The runtime is younger, was not validated with React Native 0.86 or Hermes V1, and Android may need a newer compileSdk or AGP through expo-build-properties. Figma art can be imported, but the animation and state machine must be authored in Rive by someone who owns that tool.

nodes.label: Reanimated 4
nodes.source_location: 1.2 UI interactions / layout / gesture motion: Reanimated 4 + Gesture Handler
nodes.rationale: Choice for UI interaction, layout, and gesture motion. Expo 57 pins react-native-reanimated 4.5.1 together with react-native-worklets 0.10.1. Install with npx expo install, not a hand-picked version. Worklets run on the UI thread, so animation does not depend on the JS thread. Keep at most about 100 simultaneously animated components on low-end Android, versus about 500 on iOS. CSS-style animations are cheaper for fire-and-forget motion but cannot follow live input. Layout animations are the most expensive feature on low-end Android and should stay off long lists. The cost is a native module plus some APK size and startup RAM, accepted because gestures and layout transitions need it. react-native-gesture-handler about 2.32 is required by Reanimated gestures and the bottom sheet. The app uses softwareKeyboardLayoutMode pan; PIN and amount screens add react-native-keyboard-controller 1.21.9.

nodes.label: Honi
nodes.rationale: Mascot: a glossy orange planet-bee with a ring, glow, and sparkles. It should react to app state (idle, happy, thinking, sad, and input). The Figma Emotes component set, node 653:706, has nine variants: honi idle, honi wave, bill, Phone, Secure, success, fail, alert, and question. Each is a body plus a face frame with eyes and a mouth. The MCP reported no keyframe data, so motion between variants is probably a Smart Animate prototype whose duration, delay, easing, and loop cannot be read. Which variants actually animate, and which screen uses which mood, was still open. Glow and ring may miss the 300 KB mascot budget. Planned component is src/components/mascot/Mascot.tsx with mood and size props, a Reanimated idle float, an optional lazy Lottie clip, and a static frame when reduced motion is on or the clip fails. useMascot maps typing, success, error, and idle timeout to a mood in JS rather than a state machine.

nodes.label: DRAFTS-HONEBILL
nodes.rationale: Figma file QvLzQR9hWs96dBf84A2z5C. The designer works only in Figma, and the MCP was connected on 2026-10-23. Nodes: all designs 902:6640, brand guide 942:3753, logos 902:6641. Screen frames are 402 by 874. When Motion was checked, the designs page had no real mascot or UI animation, and get_motion_context returned nothing for Wave (644:1861), Idle (644:1454), and halo (644:982). Those sets look like pose variants, so the animation is likely a prototype that swaps variants.

nodes.label: 2 GB Android device floor
nodes.rationale: The performance gate is a phone with about 2 GB of RAM running Android 8, 9, or 10. iOS and Android are built in one codebase; iOS is checked through EAS builds because this machine has no Mac. Targets: no sustained drops below 55 fps on mascot screens, cold start not regressed by more than 300 ms versus the Phase 0 baseline, and no memory growth after repeated visits. Measure a release build. Dev mode and Expo Go numbers are only indicative. MP4 and GIF references are too heavy for these devices.

nodes.label: Low-end animation budget
nodes.rationale: One live Lottie instance, the mascot. Micro-animations play once, then unmount or pause. Pause on blur and when the app is backgrounded. Animate only transform and opacity; do not animate width, height, top, or left, and do not call setState per frame. No Reanimated layout animations inside long lists. If the OS remove-animations setting is on, or the device is flagged low-end, show a static mascot frame. Each animation file targets at most 150 KB, the mascot at most 300 KB, and all animation assets at most 1 MB. Load clips per screen, not at startup. Avoid expo-blur on Android 8-10. Skia is not adopted. The Glass darkmode effect is out of scope because there is no dark mode. Brand-card inner shadows are not supported by React Native and should be gradient overlays or exported card art.

nodes.label: Mock-data frontend boundary
nodes.rationale: The frontend is built against mock data while _legacy stays untouched, as CLAUDE.md requires. src/mocks holds typed fixtures and src/hooks returns the same shape the real API will use. Never import _legacy. The navigation graph in this phase makes no real auth or Stellar calls. Session state stays in React context. Zustand is only for cross-screen UI state if needed. No Redux, and no form library until one is proven necessary.

nodes.label: Frontend UI stack choices
nodes.rationale: Keep @react-navigation/native and native-stack; add bottom-tabs only if the design needs tabs. Native stack transitions are platform-driven. Lists use @shopify/flash-list 2.0.2, which Expo bundles and which supports the New Architecture, for transactions and contacts. Bottom sheet is @gorhom/bottom-sheet only after Reanimated 4 compatibility is checked, otherwise a small custom sheet. Haptics use expo-haptics and must respect reduced-motion and haptic settings. Images use expo-image at fixed sizes. Styling stays StyleSheet.create plus a theme tokens module for colors, spacing, radius, and typography, seeded from the brand guide. Spacing and radius were not in the brand guide and have to be read off the screens.

nodes.label: Keep react-native-worklets
nodes.rationale: Keep react-native-worklets as a direct dependency, pinned to Expo's 0.10.1. Reanimated 4 does not bundle it. It is a required peer, so removing it would break the Reanimated install. This corrects the earlier assumption that Reanimated pulls worklets in.

nodes.label: mobile-ci Node 22
nodes.rationale: Task 0.3 found that mobile-ci.yml already pins Node 22, done in commit 6f88868, so the frontend-stack work did not need to change that workflow.

nodes.label: SVG and PNG asset split
nodes.rationale: Finding on 2026-10-23: Figma exports of Honi, the honeycomb art, and the card art are SVGs full of filters (drop shadow, inner shadow, blur) and masks, which React Native does not render. Decorative and mascot art is therefore PNG under assets/mascot and assets/landing. Only plain-path icons are drawn with react-native-svg, and those stay static, with no per-frame SVG animation. honi-wave.png is 569 KB at 3x, over the 300 KB mascot budget, and landing/background.png is 440 KB. Revisit with WebP or a lower scale when measuring on the 2 GB device. The honeycomb motif on Landing and cards is a static image, not a per-frame animation.

nodes.label: Built v2 screens
nodes.rationale: As of 2026-10-23 the mock onboarding flow was built: Landing, Login with Keypad and PinDots, Input Number, OTP, User Details, MPIN Creation, and Account Confirmation. Any complete OTP or PIN is accepted, nothing is saved, and a swipe returns to Login until Home exists. MPIN is not verified; the filled-dot style and gradient phone-pill border are assumptions. Home Online and Offline are one HomeScreen switched by tapping the cards; that mode is mock state, not real connectivity. BottomNavBar and MainTabs exist, with a spinning scan ring. Inbox, Transactions, and Profile were still coming-soon placeholders. Send, receive, and QR were not built. Send 3 is layered after Send 4, so the real sequence still needs the designer to confirm it. Approximations to review include single diagonal gradient headings, step-diamond overlay order, and no backdrop-blur. Gesture Handler and @react-native-masked-view/masked-view were added and are bundled in Expo Go.

nodes.label: Expo Go preview
nodes.rationale: The owner runs the app on a phone with Expo Go and no adb. Expo Go is a dev-mode runtime, so its numbers are indicative only and are not the Phase 0 release baseline. It cannot load Rive, so a Rive go/no-go spike still needs a dev client or EAS build. Start with npx expo start --go, because expo-dev-client is installed and otherwise makes expo start target a dev client. Screens, theme, fonts, and Reanimated can be previewed in Expo Go when the native package is bundled there. This machine had no Android SDK or adb, no android folder under apps/mobile, and JDK 21 installed. The release baseline for cold start, idle RAM, and APK size was still pending. The 2026-10-23 Android export baseline was 828 modules and 1.9 MB of Hermes bytecode.

nodes.label: live.honebill.app
nodes.rationale: The pending on-device memory check is adb shell dumpsys meminfo live.honebill.app. The clean-slate note still says the Android package id is live.pijin.app, so this id may be a later rename, a planned id, or a typo in the measurement command.

nodes.label: Offline E-Wallet
nodes.rationale: Product line named in the Figma brand guide. It shows Online Balance and Offline Balance cards with a Syncing chip. The logo is a bee-planet icon plus a cubic Honebill wordmark, which is a vector rather than a font, in four variants: icon, wordmark, stacked, and horizontal. Motifs are a honeycomb hexagon pattern, an orange-to-red gradient, and the glossy glow on Honi. Four line tab icons are likely Home, Inbox, Transactions, and Profile.

nodes.label: Lexend
nodes.rationale: UI font. The brand guide specifies Lexend Bold for headings, plus Regular and Light. Medium was added because the buttons use it. Loaded per weight through @expo-google-fonts/lexend, four TTF files at about 315 KB, with expo-font, and the splash is held until the fonts load. Ship only those weights. Seed colors include background #ECF0F3, white #F7F7FB, black #222021, orange #F08F31, coral #E6795E, and card gradient stops #FFCC00, #FF8800, and #EB7124. Coral and the variable named D red share the same hex, so they may be one token.

nodes.label: Rive React Native docs
nodes.rationale: Cited runtime docs at https://rive.app/docs/runtimes/react-native/react-native and the Expo install guide at https://rive.app/docs/runtimes/react-native/adding-rive-to-expo.md.

nodes.label: Reanimated performance guide
nodes.rationale: Cited at https://docs.swmansion.com/react-native-reanimated/docs/guides/performance for the low-end Android limit of about 100 simultaneous animations. Pinned versions were also read from node_modules/expo/bundledNativeModules.json for Expo 57.
